title: bug: the ps1 hot reload nests a new wrapper per script change, so seats accumulate blocked PowerShell parents (5.5 GB after one night)
description: Measured by the governor on 2026-09-19 06:50Z. df42861 made the ps1 self-restart hand over with the call operator so the reloaded wrapper keeps its console, which fixed the duplicate-seat bug from Start-Process. The cost is that every moe-agent.ps1 change leaves the old wrapper blocked on its child forever, one extra process per seat per change. After one night of landings that touched the launchers, this project had 45 seat wrappers alive, 6.2 GB working set, of which 38 were blocked reload parents holding 5.5 GB. Depth per seat was 5 to 8. Nothing bounds it inside a session, and it cannot be cleaned up piecemeal: killing an intermediate parent unblocks ITS parent, which resumes the claim loop while the innermost wrapper is still live, which is the duplicate-seat failure df42861 fixed. Today the only safe cleanup is stopping a seat's whole process tree and relaunching it. Wanted: a hand-over that does not nest, for example a thin supervisor that launches the agent script once per iteration so a reload is just the next iteration reading the new file, while the console and the one-loop-per-seat guarantee are preserved. The sh twin exec()s in place and has no such growth, so this is a ps1-only defect; keep the twins behaviourally equal.
definitionOfDone: A moe-agent.ps1 hot reload leaves no blocked parent: after N script changes a seat still has exactly one wrapper process, proven by a postflight arm that counts wrapper processes across two reloads
The reload still keeps the seat's console and never produces a second claim loop for the same worker id (the df42861 regression stays covered)
parity-check.{sh,ps1} pass and the sh twin's exec hand-over is unchanged

implementationPlan.description:
RED FIRST: a hot-reload arm in scripts/tests/postflight.ps1, the only harness that runs the ps1 wrapper. This task waits on task-d1441364, which edits the same two files, so find code by function name.

Arm 'hot reload keeps one wrapper process':
1. Copy the repo's scripts/ into a temp root, plus docs/roles if the wrapper loads role docs from there, so the arm edits a COPY and never the live launcher.
2. Run the copied moe-agent.ps1 with -Loop -PollInterval 1 against the existing fake proxy, with FAKE_CLAIM_MODE=idle and MOE_DISABLE_HEARTBEAT=1, via Start-Process -PassThru with redirected output.
3. Wait for the first logged claim_next_task.
4. Twice: append a comment line ('# reload N') to the copied moe-agent.ps1. Wait until the fake's deregister.log shows a 'wrapper_restart' deregister AND a later claim is logged. Then count wrapper processes: Win32_Process whose CommandLine contains the copied script path and whose executable is pwsh or powershell. The heartbeat job is disabled, so it is not counted.
5. Stop the whole tree (taskkill /T /F), as the loop arms do.

Assertions:
(a) exactly 2 wrapper_restart deregisters;
(b) exactly 1 wrapper process after EACH reload;
(c) every claim_next_task across both reloads carries ONE runner identity (processStartedAt/host) — one process, one claim loop;
(d) at least one claim after the second reload, so the seat keeps working.

On today's wrapper it must FAIL: each reload spawns `& $exe @args` and blocks, so (b) sees 2 and then 3 processes, and (c) sees three identities. Run it on pwsh 7 AND PS 5.1, launched from PowerShell, never from Git Bash, and paste both failures. The sh harness gets no arm: the sh twin execs in place and is unchanged by this task.

Evidence log is the fake's .moe/evidence-rpcs.jsonl (there is no deregister.log): mapped to c=claim, r=wrapper_restart deregister, x=other deregister. Edit 1 REWRITES the restart announcement to '... (edit 1 loaded)' (proves the reloaded pass runs the bytes on disk: pass 2 prints it at reload 2); edit 2 appends '# reload 2'. Writes retry (the seat's own hash read can refuse a write). Process count = Win32_Process pwsh.exe/powershell.exe whose CommandLine contains the unique copied path. Assertions collected then thrown together: sequence ^c+rc+rc+$ (a: exactly two wrapper_restart, no other deregister; d: claims after reload 2), counts '1,1' (b), one processStartedAt|host (c), edited-bytes line. Tree stopped with taskkill /T /F + a Stop-Process sweep of any match.

- pwsh 7.6.6: 'HOT RELOAD FAILED: expected exactly 1 wrapper process after each reload; counted 2 then 3 | expected every claim to carry one runner identity; got 3: 11632@...|yaron-pc; 38828@...|yaron-pc; 48924@...|yaron-pc' (6 s)
- PS 5.1.26100: same two failures, 'counted 2 then 3', 'got 3' (5 s)
No reload wrapper processes leaked afterwards.

FINDING (scope growth for step 2, same block of moe-agent.ps1): when Windows PowerShell 5.1 is launched by node under pwsh, which is exactly how CI runs the 5.1 leg ('node postflight-safe.mjs powershell' inside a pwsh step), PSModulePath carries pwsh's module dirs and 'Get-FileHash' is NOT RECOGNIZED (probe: 'The term 'Get-FileHash' is not recognized'). The wrapper's restart check catches that and fails open, so hot reload is silently OFF there: the same arm via node->powershell on HEAD's wrapper timed out with 'RPC sequence ccccccccccccccccccccccccccc' (27 claims, no reload). A direct pwsh->powershell launch resets PSModulePath, which is why fed8c0f saw it only on CI. Step 2 therefore also swaps the two Get-FileHash calls for .NET SHA-256, otherwise this arm would be red on CI's 5.1 leg forever.

Non-nesting hand-over in scripts/moe-agent.ps1:
- In-process supervisor right after param(), before $ErrorActionPreference (comment carries the why + the 45 wrappers / 6.2 GB / 5.5 GB measurement). Loop: $global:MoeWrapperReload=$false; $global:LASTEXITCODE=0; & $PSCommandPath @PSBoundParameters; $moeRc=$LASTEXITCODE; while the pass set MoeWrapperReload. finally resets $global:MoeWrapperSupervised.
- Deviation from the plan's catch (kept its outcome): the relaunch hint prints only when a reload happened, then the error is RETHROWN (exit 1 + the original error record). The plan's catch-all would have relabelled every FIRST-pass terminating error (e.g. EAP=Stop Write-Error 'Moe proxy script not found') as 'wrapper relaunch failed' on stdout.
- Bottom hand-over is now `if ($script:MoeWrapperRelaunchRequested) { $global:MoeWrapperReload = $true }` + an unconditional `exit 0` (so normal completion never hands the supervisor a stale native exit code; -File used to give 0 there). In-loop hash check / deregister 'wrapper_restart' / break unchanged.
- $script:MoeWrapperHostExe, $script:MoeWrapperRelaunchArgs and their capture deleted (grep: no reads left). Hand-over comments rewritten (one process + one console per seat; runner identity survives the reload so a held attempt can still reattach).
- SCOPE GROWTH (same block, found in step 1): the two Get-FileHash calls became Get-MoeWrapperHash (.NET SHA-256 over ReadAllBytes, disposed). Under node->powershell (CI's 5.1 leg) Get-FileHash is 'not recognized', so hot reload was silently off there and the new arm could never pass in CI.

- pwsh 7.6.6: '[hot reload] ok: 2 reloads, 1 wrapper process, 1 runner identity', PASS, 5 s
- PS 5.1: same, 5 s
- PS 5.1 via node (CI shape): same (was a 30 s timeout with 27 claims and no reload before)
- kept log: one identity 48964@639254268681893035 across all 3 passes, '(edit 1 loaded)' printed by pass 2, RPC sequence c r c r c.
Exit codes through the supervisor: -Loop -NoLoop = 2 (pwsh + 5.1); first-pass terminating error = 1 with the original error and no hint (both); reload into an unparseable file (appended 'function Broken {') = hint 'wrapper relaunch failed; the seat is stopped, relaunch it by hand: ... Missing closing '}'' + exit 1, one wrapper_restart deregister (both engines).
Live-fleet check during the edits: only 3 ps1 wrappers were running (architect-74607b1b, worker-0966ef4c, governor-daa92494), all blocked inside CLI runs, so none reloaded into an intermediate state. Their next reload still goes through their OLD hand-over (one last nested parent each), then the child runs this supervisor.

implementationPlan.description:
PROCESS-GLOBAL STATE that a same-process rerun would otherwise accumulate or freeze. Both are in scripts/moe-agent.ps1.

1. PowerShell.Exiting subscriber (Register-EngineEvent near the top). Each run would add another subscriber bound to its own, now dead, script scope. Before registering, run `Unregister-Event -SourceIdentifier PowerShell.Exiting -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` (this process has no other subscriber to it), then register as today. Exactly one handler, the current run's, deregisters the current worker on window close.
2. Add-Type of MoeFrozenGateProcess. A compiled type lives as long as the process, so after an in-process reload a CHANGED C# definition would silently keep the old code.
   - Name the class after its definition: keep a placeholder in $script:MoeGateProcessDefinition, and set $script:MoeGateTypeName = 'MoeFrozenGateProcess' + the first 12 hex digits of SHA256(the definition text).
   - Substitute that name into the definition, and have Initialize-MoeGateProcess test `$script:MoeGateTypeName -as [type]` before calling Add-Type.
   - Create instances with New-Object -TypeName $script:MoeGateTypeName -ArgumentList @(...).
   An unchanged definition reuses the loaded type. A changed one compiles a new name.
3. Confirm everything else is per run and needs nothing: env vars are set each run and cleaned in the finally; the heartbeat Start-Job is stopped in the finally; the $global:OutputEncoding swap is restored inside Invoke-MoeRpc; TreatControlCAsInput=$false is idempotent. Say so in the step note.
implementationPlan.note:
Process-global state in scripts/moe-agent.ps1:
1. PowerShell.Exiting: before registering, remove only OUR previous subscriber (Get-EventSubscriber -SourceIdentifier PowerShell.Exiting | Where action text matches 'Invoke-MoeDeregister' | Unregister-Event -SubscriptionId + Remove-Job of its event job), inside try/catch, then register as today. Deviation from the plan's unconditional `Unregister-Event -SourceIdentifier PowerShell.Exiting`: moe-team.ps1 launches `powershell -NoExit -Command ".\moe-agent.ps1 ..."` WITHOUT -NoProfile, so an operator profile can own its own Exiting handler; the targeted filter never touches it. Probe (supervisor mimic, 3 passes, both engines): without cleanup subscribers/jobs grow 1,2,3; with it 1,1,1.
   MEASURED CAVEAT, now in the comment: the action resolves Invoke-MoeDeregister only while the registering pass is on the stack. Under the supervisor, at process exit after the pass returned, the action runs but gets "The term 'Invoke-Dereg' is not recognized" (pwsh 7.6.6 and PS 5.1, even with ONE pass). A plain -File launch dot-sources into global scope, which is why it resolved before; the IDE launches (JetBrains `-Command "& <script>"`, VS Code -EncodedCommand, moe-team `-Command .\moe-agent.ps1`) were already in this state. The outer finally stays the deregister of record (the wrapper's teardown comments already say a window close runs nothing). Deleting the handler is a candidate follow-up; kept per plan.
2. Gate type: `$script:MoeGateTypeName = 'MoeFrozenGateProcess' + first 12 hex of SHA-256(definition text)`; the class's own name is the placeholder (`.Replace('MoeFrozenGateProcess', $script:MoeGateTypeName)` at Add-Type); Initialize-MoeGateProcess tests `$script:MoeGateTypeName -as [type]`; the call site is `New-Object -TypeName $script:MoeGateTypeName -ArgumentList @(...)`. The .NET SHA from step 2 became the shared Get-MoeSha256Hex([byte[]]) defined above the gate definition (needed at load time), also used by both restart-hash sites; Get-MoeWrapperHash removed. Probe (AST-loaded wrapper statements in ONE process, both engines): name MoeFrozenGateProcessEA79CE2AF7AB on both; unchanged definition -> assemblies 73->73 (pwsh) / 19->19 (5.1), no second compile; the renamed type ran a gate child (exit 7); a changed definition -> MoeFrozenGateProcessCDBFECEED32E, exit 3, new member Probe=42 live.
3. Everything else is per run: env vars are set each pass (CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS removed and GROK_* restored in the outer finally; the rest are what the old child process inherited anyway); the heartbeat Start-Job is stopped after each CLI run and by Invoke-MoeDeregister (Stop-Job + Remove-Job) in the finally and on the restart path; $global:OutputEncoding and [Console]::OutputEncoding swaps are restored in their finally blocks; Push-Location/Pop-Location are paired; TreatControlCAsInput=$false is idempotent; $global:LASTEXITCODE is reset by the supervisor per pass; the AST scan finds no other $global: writes and there is no other Add-Type.
Re-verified after these edits: the reload-only arm is green on pwsh 7, PS 5.1 and PS 5.1 via node.

comments.author: governor-39911495
comments.content: Governor data point for the implementer (2026-09-19 09:05Z): the growth is driven by edits, not only by landings. Idle seats poll every 30 s, and each poll checks the moe-agent.ps1 hash, so every SAVE a worker makes to the repo copy while developing reloads every idle ps1 seat, one nesting level each. Between 09:02:58Z and 09:04:48Z, while task-d1441364's worker was editing moe-agent.ps1, qa-7100be29, qa-5e66a826 and qa-9a371c33 each reloaded (wrapper_restart), taking this project from 45 to 48 seat wrappers with 41 blocked parents. Free RAM went from 22.6 GB to 19.0 GB over the morning. Two consequences for the plan: (1) once the hand-over stops nesting, a reload storm during development costs nothing, so fix the nesting first; (2) if the design keeps any per-reload cost, reload only when the hash has been stable for a short window, so a burst of saves costs one reload, not N. Keep the one-loop-per-seat and keep-the-console guarantees from df42861.

comments.author: worker-0966ef4c
comments.content:
SELF-REVIEW (worker-0966ef4c), final bytes of scripts/moe-agent.ps1 + scripts/tests/postflight.ps1:

1. Two claim loops for one seat? No. One process runs one supervisor, and `&` blocks until the pass returns. A pass returns only after its loop broke, its outer finally ran and the seat deregistered with 'wrapper_restart'. The arm pins this: 1 wrapper process after each of 2 reloads, 1 runner identity on every claim, RPC sequence ^c+rc+rc+$. Still possible and unchanged: an operator starting a second wrapper with the same -WorkerId. Transition: a seat running pre-change bytes hands over once more through its OLD `& <exe>` relaunch, so it keeps one last blocked parent. Its child runs the supervisor and never nests again. The old parent only exits when that child exits; it never resumes a loop.
2. Ctrl+C inside the rerun boundary: the host stops the pipeline. The pass's outer finally runs (rescue, deregister, cleanup) and the supervisor's finally resets the flag. Only the bottom-of-file line after a restart break sets MoeWrapperReload, so there is no reload. The frozen interrupt-int arm passed through the supervised pass on pwsh and PS 5.1.
3. Stale PowerShell.Exiting handler: the cleanup targets only OUR subscriber and its event job. A probe on both engines gave 1,2,3 subscribers and jobs without it and 1,1,1 with it. It is targeted rather than a blanket `Unregister-Event -SourceIdentifier` because moe-team.ps1 launches with a profile, which may own a handler. MEASURED CAVEAT: the action resolves Invoke-MoeDeregister only while the pass that registered it is on the stack. At process exit after that pass returned, it fails with "is not recognized" (both engines, even with one pass). IDE launches (`-Command "& <script>"`) were already in that state. So a handler can never deregister the wrong run, and the outer finally stays the deregister of record. Candidate follow-up: delete the handler.
4. Gate C#: the type name is 'MoeFrozenGateProcess' plus the first 12 hex digits of SHA-256(definition). In-process probe on both engines:
   - Unchanged definition: no second compile (assemblies 73->73 on pwsh, 19->19 on 5.1).
   - Changed definition: a new name compiles, and its new member is live (Probe=42).
   - The renamed type ran real gate children (exit 7 and exit 3).
   - The frozen gate arms are green on both engines.
5. Exit codes:
   - -Loop -NoLoop exits 2 on both engines.
   - Every `exit N` in the body returns N, and the supervisor exits N.
   - Normal completion is now an explicit `exit 0`; under -File it was an implicit 0.
   - A first-pass terminating error is rethrown: exit 1 with the original error and no relaunch hint.
   - A reload into an unparseable file prints 'wrapper relaunch failed; the seat is stopped, relaunch it by hand: ... Missing closing '}'' and exits 1.
   - Full postflight and the node tests (61/61) cover the rest.
6. PS 5.1: `-Interactive:$false` (passed via -Command) stays BOUND in the next pass on both engines (ContainsKey True, value False), so the architect/governor opt-out survives a reload. Arrays are preserved. After `exit 7` in the last pass, $LASTEXITCODE is 7 and the process exits 7 on both engines. Pre-existing and unchanged: a -File launch with `-Interactive:$false` typed at a pwsh prompt fails the OUTER bind on 5.1.
7. The sh twin is untouched. `git diff --stat -- scripts/` shows only moe-agent.ps1 (116 lines changed) and tests/postflight.ps1 (+84). The sh diff is empty. parity-check passes on sh, pwsh and 5.1.

Found beyond the plan:
- (a) Under node->powershell (CI's 5.1 leg), Get-FileHash is "not recognized", so HEAD never hot-reloads there. The same arm on HEAD's wrapper timed out after 27 claims with no reload. Both hash sites now use .NET SHA-256 (the shared Get-MoeSha256Hex). The exact CI command `node scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs powershell` returns failureClass NONE.
- (b) Added the guard `-and $PSCommandPath`: a file-less invocation runs the body directly, as before, instead of failing on `& ''`.
- (c) `&` re-invokes fine through a path containing '[1]' and a space, on both engines, via -File and -Command.
- (d) The arm against the real pre-df42861 wrapper (Start-Process detach) FAILS on both engines ("RPC sequence 'cx'": a terminal_closed deregister, then the wrapper exited), so the df42861 regression stays covered.

Final full runs on the final bytes (MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_SEC=400): pwsh 557 s and PS 5.1 529 s, both 'PASS frozen candidate scenarios: 69', '[hot reload] ok', 'commit-scope scenarios run: 30', 'PASS postflight.ps1'.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
- A separate thin supervisor file with the body in moe-agent-core.ps1: rejected. It changes what the JetBrains/VS Code bundles, parity-check, the harnesses and the docs point at, for the same effect as the in-file prologue.
- Start-Process -NoNewWindow followed by the parent exiting: rejected. The launching shell returns to its prompt while the child writes to the same console, which is the dead-looking-seat confusion df42861 fixed.
- Recursing into the script in-process at the bottom (`& $PSCommandPath` without a loop): rejected. It still nests call frames and scopes per reload, and it would reach PowerShell's call-depth limit over a long run.
- Keeping the child-process relaunch and reaping old parents: rejected. Killing an intermediate parent resumes ITS parent's loop, which is the duplicate-seat failure.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- Today's hand-over is at the bottom of moe-agent.ps1: after the outer finally, `& $moeRelaunchExe @moeRelaunchArgs; exit $LASTEXITCODE`. The parent blocks for the child's whole life.
- The restart check sits at the top of each loop iteration: hash change, then Invoke-MoeDeregister 'wrapper_restart', then break.
- Process-global side effects in the body:
  - Register-EngineEvent PowerShell.Exiting near the top: accumulates on every run.
  - Add-Type of MoeFrozenGateProcess (guarded by -as [type], used through New-Object by name): would freeze old C# after a reload.
  - Everything else is per run.
- The param block has no ValueFromRemainingArguments, so @PSBoundParameters forwards everything.
- No test covers the self-restart today (task-e92b2cb3 is in BACKLOG).
- The runner identity is <pid>@<start token>, so an in-process reload keeps it, which is better for reattach than a new child PID.
planningNotes.risks:
- The arm must edit a COPY of the wrapper, never the live scripts/moe-agent.ps1: repo-launched seats hot-reload on every edit of that file (mem:moes-installed-plugin-staleness).
- Process counting under fleet load: match on the unique copied script path and on the pwsh or powershell executable only, and poll with a deadline rather than a fixed sleep.
- PS 5.1 differences: the $global variable scoping, `exit` inside a script invoked with &, and splatting SwitchParameter values. Test both engines.
- A reload that changes the param() block can fail to bind the old parameters; that is the same outcome as today's child relaunch, and the catch keeps it a clear stop.
- dependsOn task-d1441364, which edits the same two files. Re-check git status before editing.

completionSummary:
ps1 hot reload no longer nests. scripts/moe-agent.ps1 has an in-process supervisor right after param(). The first invocation runs each pass with `& $PSCommandPath @PSBoundParameters` and loops while a pass sets $global:MoeWrapperReload. The bottom hand-over sets that flag and then does `exit 0`. The old `& <exe> <GetCommandLineArgs>` child relaunch and its HostExe/RelaunchArgs capture are gone. Result: one process and one console per seat across reloads, and the runner identity survives a reload.
